partners.mechanism_chain: MVK (HGNC:7500) —DISRUPTS→ Mevalonate Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1432186); Mevalonate Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1432186) —DECREASES→ Isopentenyl pyrophosphate (CHEBI:40733); Isopentenyl pyrophosphate (CHEBI:40733) —LEADS_TO→ Periodic fever (HP:0012427); Isopentenyl pyrophosphate (CHEBI:40733) —LEADS_TO→ Elevated IgD (HP:0030172); MVK (HGNC:7500) —LEADS_TO→ Fever (HP:0000976). Loss-of-function mutations in MVK lead to a deficiency in mevalonate kinase, disrupting the mevalonate pathway. This results in decreased production of downstream isoprenoids like isopentenyl pyrophosphate. The accumulation of upstream metabolites and/or deficiency of downstream products contributes to the inflammatory phenotype seen in both periodic fever and elevated IgD, which are characteristic of HIDS and MVD respectively. The fever phenotype is directly linked to the MVK defect, while the elevated IgD is a downstream consequence of the disrupted pathway, possibly through altered cytokine signaling.

This deficiency impacts cellular processes in multiple tissues, manifesting as failure to thrive in Mevalonate Kinase Deficiency and abnormal keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation in disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis 3.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MVK with a clear gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease, or evidence that the mevalonate pathway is not significantly impacted in affected individuals. _(variant: rs121908117 (c.797C>T, p.Ala266Val) in MVK has a low frequency in gnomAD, consistent with a rare pathogenic variant.)_
